chunks: The Commander of the Faithful, ʿAlī عليه السلام, said:
"The initiation of salat (prayer) is wudu (ablution), its prohibition is the takbir, and its release is the taslim."

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: the closing salutation that concludes the prayer
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: the opening declaration of magnification, saying Allahu Akbar
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: ritual ablution required as purification before prayer
key_terms.تَحْرِيمُهَا: that by which ordinary acts become forbidden during prayer
key_terms.تَحْلِيلُهَا: that by which prayer is ended and restrictions are lifted

ai.seo_question: What marks the beginning, binding start, and ending of salat (prayer) in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the formal entry, binding commencement, and completion of salat (prayer). It identifies wudu (ablution) as its opening prerequisite, the takbir as the point at which prohibited acts become forbidden within prayer, and the taslim as the act by which prayer is concluded.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.68 - The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), said:
"The initiation of prayer is purification (ablution), its prohibition is the takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar'), and its permissibility is the Tasleem (saying 'Assalamu Alaikum')."
